definition: A decorator is a function that takes another function as an argument, extends its behavior without modifying it and returns the modified version.
invariants: A decorator always takes a callable object (function or class) as input.
Decorators can only modify functions' behaviors, not classes or other objects.
The original function's signature remains unchanged after being wrapped by the decorator.
constraints: A decorator must always return a callable object (function or class).
Decorators are applied to functions using '@' syntax and can only be used at the time of function definition.
Only one decorator can be applied per function.
